categories.title: Getting Started
categories.desc: Your first golem, start to finish, and how to read this book.

pages.text:
This manual covers everything about Golem Garage: every part, every material, the Garage, power, jobs and Cubs.

Golems are built from five parts. Each part is a §lshape§r (what it does) made from a §lmaterial§r (how strong it is). The golem looks exactly like what it's made of: iron arms are iron, gold legs are gold.

§lReading the book§r

- Click a chapter, then an entry.
- Arrows at the bottom corners turn pages; so do the scroll wheel and the arrow keys.
- The middle button goes back; right-click or Backspace does too.
- The top button goes home.
- Hover any item to see it.

Items with a blue "Click to read" line open their own entry.
- Search from the home page.

The book reopens where you left it.

A complete golem takes about ten minutes and some cobblestone, redstone and a little iron.

§l1.§r Craft a Golem Frame. §l2.§r Place it. §l3.§r Craft parts and right-click the frame with each one. §l4.§r Give it a core so it has power. §l5.§r Open its panel and give it a job.
pages.title: Ten Minutes to a Golem

pages.text: Cobblestone in a ring with redstone in the middle. The bottom middle stays empty.
pages.title: Golem Frame

pages.text: Place the frame on the ground. It's a bare metal skeleton: it follows you, but it is slow and weak until you fit parts.
pages.title: The Bare Frame

pages.text: Every part is crafted the same way: the material goes in the M spots. Stone parts use cobblestone and are the cheapest. Right-click the golem with a part to fit it.
pages.title: Stone Stub Legs

pages.text: The core holds power. Without one the golem works, but 25% slower. A Redstone Core needs a redstone block in the middle.
pages.title: Redstone Core

pages.text: Fit a head, torso, arms and legs too. Here is a stone golem with an iron core: cheap, slow, and a fine helper for your first night.
pages.title: A Starter Golem

pages.text:
Right-click the golem with an empty hand to open its §lpanel§r.

The §lStatus§r tab shows a 3D view, each part with its durability bar and a button to remove it, health, power, armor, damage, speed, sight and carrying space, what it's doing right now, and its recent activity.

The §lRules§r tab is where you teach it jobs.
pages.title: The Panel

pages.text:
§lPress G§r while looking at a golem (or shift + right-click it with an empty hand) to pick it up as an item. It keeps its parts, wear, rules, links, name and everything it carries. Right-click the ground to place it again.

§lUpgrading§r is just fitting a better part: the old one comes back to you with its wear intact.
pages.title: Picking Up and Upgrading

rows: Pick the golem up as an item. The G key does the same.
Fit it. The old part comes back to you.
Repair a quarter of every part and health.
Wax copper parts so they stop aging.
Scrape one stage of oxidation off copper.
Give it the Linker's marks. Shift: clear its links.
Record its build, or rebuild it from one.
Right-click a Garage Controller to repair it.
pages.title: Right-click a Golem With...

pages.text: Every player gets one copy the first time they join. Lost it? Craft another from a book and an iron ingot.

categories.title: Golem Anatomy
categories.desc: How a golem's five parts add up: slots, stats, scaling and set bonuses.

pages.text: Every golem has five slots. Each can hold one part, and each part shows on the golem in its own material.
pages.title: Five Slots

rows: Sight range (how far it notices hostiles and crops) and a little health. Shapes add light, sealing or long sight.
Most of the health and how many stacks it carries. Shapes add smelting or sealing.
Damage and work speed. The shape decides which jobs it can do.
Speed, step height and knockback resistance. Shapes add climbing, wheels or treads.
Power capacity and how it recharges. Its color is the glow of the eyes and core window. The core sits on the golem's back.
pages.title: What Each Slot Does

pages.text:
§lEmpty slots§r show the bare frame and work poorly:

- No legs: 30% slower.
- No arms: weak 2-damage hits and half work speed.
- No head: sees only 6 blocks.
- No torso: carries 9 stacks.
- No core: no power system at all, and 25% slower.
pages.title: Missing Parts

rows: 20 for the frame, plus each part's health. At zero the golem breaks down; it never dies.
The arms' damage plus 1.5 per tier.
Shown as a percent of a normal golem. Legs and material set it.
The head's sight plus 2 per tier. A broken head sees 4 blocks.
Inventory stacks, from the torso. Tier 5+ torsos carry 9 more (up to 36).
From the core. Used by moving, hitting and working.
How fast jobs go: hauling, harvesting, smelting. From the arms.
pages.title: Reading the Panel

pages.text:
§lHow tier scales a part§r

- Durability: (60 + 40 x tier) x material durability x slot factor (head 0.8, torso 1.2, arms 1.0, legs 1.0, core 0.9).
- Health: shape health x (1 + 0.3 x tier).
- Armor:
pages.title: The Formulas

pages.text:
0.8 x tier.
- Damage: shape damage + 1.5 x tier.
- Power: shape power x (1 + 0.25 x tier) x material power.
- Sight: shape sight + 2 x tier.
- Work: shape work x (1 + 0.1 x tier) x material work.
All five parts in the same material make a §lmatched set§r: +10% speed, 10% less wear, and Garage repairs 20% faster. The panel shows "Set!".
pages.title: Matched Set

pages.text:
§lGarage kit§r
Three or more steel-family parts (Steel, Crimson Steel, Tyrian Steel): Garage repairs 20% faster. This stacks with a matched set.

§lDesert kit§r
Visor Head + Sealed Hold + Tread Legs: no part wears in rain or desert sand, sealed or not.
pages.title: Other Sets

pages.text: A steel desert kit: visor, sealed hold and treads, with claws and a solar core. It also counts as a Garage kit.

categories.title: Materials
categories.desc: Every material, what it's good for, and the traits that make some special.

pages.text:
A material is matched by its ingot §ltag§r, so any mod's version of an ingot works. A material only appears in recipes and the Parts tab when some installed mod provides it.

Higher tiers mean more health, armor, damage, power, sight and durability. Some materials also have traits: special effects listed in their entries.
pages.title: Materials

rows: Tier 2. All The Ores / Silent Gear
pages.title: By Tier

pages.text: Copper parts slowly turn exposed, weathered, then oxidized, and get 3% slower each stage. Wax with honeycomb to stop it; scrape a stage off with an axe.
pages.title: Oxidizes

categories.title: Wear and Repair
categories.desc: Parts wear out one by one. How to read the damage and fix it.

pages.text: Each part wears on its own.
pages.title: Wear You Can See

pages.text: Cracks spread across a part as it wears: this golem's head is lightly worn, its arms badly, and its legs are broken.

rows: A random part wears with each hit.
The arms wear as it hauls, harvests or smelts.
The core wears 1 per 100 power spent.
Outdoors in rain or in a desert, every unsealed part wears every 30 seconds.
pages.title: What Wears Parts

pages.text:
§lBroken parts§r stay fitted but go dark and spark:

- Head: sees 4 blocks.
- Arms: hit and work at 30%.
- Legs: half speed.
- Torso: half health, carries 9 stacks.
- Core: a quarter of its power.
pages.title: Broken Parts

pages.text:
The panel shows a red bar and you get a message when a part breaks.

§2§lTip:§r matched sets wear 10% less, and Hardened materials ignore 30% of wear.
At zero health a golem doesn't die: it §lbreaks down§r into a Broken Golem item that goes to your inventory (or drops if you aren't there).
pages.title: Breaking Down

pages.text: Nothing is lost: parts, rules, inventory, links and name all stay in the item, though every part takes 15% extra wear in the fall. Repair it in a Garage to bring it back.

§4§lCareful:§r a broken golem can't be placed until it's repaired.

A golem that loses a fight far from home: walk back with its item, or keep a Garage near where it works.
Two iron ingots and a slime ball make two kits.
pages.title: Repair Kit

pages.text:
§lRepair Kit§r: right-click a golem. Every part gets back a quarter of its durability, and it heals a quarter of its health.

§lRepair Self§r rule: the golem uses kits from its own inventory.

§lAnvil§r: a loose part item repairs with its own material, like a tool.

§lGarage§r: a full repair of everything.
pages.title: Four Ways to Repair

pages.text: Copper parts age a stage every so often (exposed, weathered, oxidized), turning green on the golem, and get 3% slower per stage.
pages.title: Waxing

pages.text: Right-click with §lhoneycomb§r to wax every copper part: waxed copper never ages. The panel shows "Wax".
Right-click with an §laxe§r to scrape copper parts: it takes the wax off first, then one stage of oxidation per use. A Garage repair polishes copper back to new and keeps the wax.
pages.title: Scraping

pages.text: Right-click a golem with vines to drape it like the iron golems of old. Shears trim them off again. Purely for looks.
pages.title: Overgrown

categories.title: The Garage
categories.desc: A repair bay you build from your own blocks. Lasers rebuild a broken golem in about two minutes.

pages.text: A Garage is a sealed room with a §lGarage Controller§r in one wall and §lLaser Emitters§r in the ceiling. Put a broken golem in and the lasers repair it.
pages.title: The Garage

pages.text:
A repair gives back every part's durability, all health and all power, and polishes copper to new.

It costs one unit of each damaged part's own material and takes 2 minutes (less with set bonuses or a Steel Emitter).
pages.title: Repairs

pages.text: While it works, the golem rides a lift into the middle of the room, hung from hoist chains, and turns slowly while the emitters take turns firing crackling red, blue, pink and amber laser bolts at it. Sparks and embers spray off where they hit, smoke drifts off its plating, and it shudders with every shot.
Top view of a 5 x 5 Garage. The controller (left) is in the wall; the emitters (cyan) are in the ceiling above the bay.
pages.title: Top View

rows: 3 to 9 blocks wide and deep, 4 to 8 blocks tall, fully enclosed.
Planks, stone, smooth stone, stone bricks, bricks, concrete, iron or copper blocks, deepslate bricks, any glass, Garage Windows and Garage Doors.
Any solid block. Glowing blocks like sea lanterns are fine. The ceiling can also be glass, for a skylight.
In a side wall, facing into the room.
2 to 4 Laser or Steel Emitters set into the ceiling, above the room's air.
pages.title: The Rules

pages.text: §lHold a Garage Controller§r and a see-through plan appears: white for walls, blue-gray for floor and ceiling, cyan for emitters, yellow for the controller, orange for the doorway, red for anything in the way. Each block vanishes from the plan as you place it, and a checklist counts what's left.
pages.title: The Build Plan

pages.text: Sneak + scroll changes the room size.

Place the controller first: the room goes the way you're facing. Keep holding a controller while you build and the plan follows it.

Right-click the controller with an §lempty hand§r to check the room.

Breaking a wall pauses a repair. Breaking the controller drops the golem out.
pages.title: Checking It

pages.text: When the room is complete it §ltransforms§r: rusty panels sweep across every wall, floor and ceiling, starting at the controller, and your blocks disappear behind a wasteland workshop.
pages.title: The Transformation

pages.text: Corrugated metal, grimy brick and bolted plates inside, a plank roof with a hoist beam, an oily concrete floor, and a weathered shell outside with spikes on the roof and a smoking exhaust stack. A workbench, tyres, oil drums and jerry cans fill the corners.
It also lights itself: hidden light blocks under the roof by the lanterns keep it bright day and night. Break any part of the room and it goes back to how you built it, lights and all.

Once complete, the emitters glow brighter, a neon §lGOLEM GARAGE§r sign flickers on outside above the controller, the lift pad gets a hazard-striped ring, yellow bay lines appear on the floor and lanterns hang from the roof.

Inside, a panel above the controller shows READY, or the repair's progress.
pages.title: Coming to Life

pages.text: During a repair amber warning lights spin inside and on the sign, and the sign counts up the percent.
Iron, an iron trapdoor and redstone make 4. Place several side by side and stacked for one big roller door.
pages.title: Garage Door

pages.text: It rolls up for golems and cubs, redstone or a right-click (right-click again to let it close).
Four glass and an iron nugget make 4. Use them, or any glass, in the walls and roof so you can watch the repairs.
pages.title: Garage Window

pages.text:
The build plan marks a 3-wide doorway in the back wall in orange: fill it with Garage Doors so golems can come and go, or with plain wall.

A door counts as wall even while it's open, so repairs keep going when a golem walks out.
pages.title: Doorways

pages.text: Iron, a lever and redstone. Goes in a wall.
A glass pane, two iron ingots and a redstone torch. Goes in the ceiling.
Upgrade a Laser Emitter with a steel ingot. One anywhere in the ceiling makes repairs 20% faster.
Two iron ingots and coal. Also a golem material of its own (tier 3, tough), and counts toward the Garage kit.

§lBy hand§r: right-click the controller holding the Broken Golem item.

§lBy itself§r: link a golem to the controller with a Golem Linker and give it a "go to Garage" rule. It walks in when the rule fires. The Medic preset does this.

Any golem can be repaired, broken down or just worn.
pages.title: Two Ways In

pages.text:
§lCost§r: one unit of each damaged part's own material: iron parts need iron ingots, gold parts need gold, stone parts cobblestone, and so on.

The Garage takes them from, in order:
- your inventory
- the golem's own inventory
- a chest or barrel next to the controller
pages.title: Paying

pages.text: §2§lTip:§r keep a chest of ingots by the controller, and a golem that walks in by itself never needs you.

categories.title: Power
categories.desc: How golems store, spend and recharge power.

pages.text:
The §lcore§r sets how much power a golem holds. It uses a little standing still, more while moving (1 every 10 seconds idle, 1 every 2 seconds walking), and one point per hit or task.

At §lzero power§r it moves at 40% speed and its eyes dim and flicker.
pages.title: Power

rows: Recharges by burning redstone it carries: a redstone block gives 100, dust gives 12 (only while below 75%). Any golem can also charge next to a placed redstone block with the Recharge action.
Recharges by burning fuel it carries, like a furnace: coal gives 80 power. It never burns an item it could smelt instead.
Charges under open sky while it rains (1 power a second) and three times faster in thunderstorms. A lightning strike fills it completely and doesn't hurt it.
Charges in daylight under open sky when it isn't raining (1 power a second).
Slowly charges anywhere, even underground (1 power every 3 seconds), and mends 1 health every 5 seconds.
Never runs out of power, but is always 25% slower.
pages.title: Recharging

pages.text:
§lRecharge action§r: walks to a placed redstone block within 12 blocks and charges next to it, whatever its core. Put "power below 20%: recharge" at the top of a worker's rules.

§lConductive§r materials (copper, signalum, azure electrum) add capacity and charge 25% faster.
pages.title: Charging Up

categories.title: Jobs and Rules
categories.desc: Teach a golem a job with WHEN / DO / UNLESS rules, or start from a preset.

pages.text:
Don't want to write rules? Click §lMode§r under the golem's picture on the Status tab:

§lAggressive§r: follows you and attacks every hostile mob within 12 blocks. §lPeaceful§r: follows you and never attacks anything, even if it's hit. §lGuard§r: follows you and only fights mobs that attack you. §lRules§r: runs its rules (the default).
pages.title: Modes

pages.text:
Any mode but Rules overrides the rules completely. The rules aren't lost: switch back to Rules and they run again.

You can also use §l/golemgarage mode <golem> <mode>§r.
pages.title: Modes and Rules

pages.text:
Open the golem's panel and go to §lRules§r. Each rule reads:

§lWHEN§r something is true
§lDO§r an action
§lUNLESS§r something else (optional)

Up to 8 rules, checked top to bottom twice a second. The §lfirst that applies§r runs and is highlighted. If none do, it follows you.
pages.title: Rules

pages.text:
Each rule reads like a sentence: "When §lpower is below 20%§r → §lrecharge§r". Click any colored part to pick from a list of choices with explanations. Click a yellow number to raise it, right-click to lower it, or scroll.

The arrows move a rule up or down; the x deletes it. Quick jobs at the top load a ready-made set.
pages.title: Editing

pages.text:
Undo puts back your last change.

Changes save when you close the panel.

§lOrder matters.§r Put urgent rules first: "power below 20%: recharge" above the job, and "always" last as the fallback.

§lUNLESS§r stops a rule even when its WHEN is true. Example: "chest A has 1 DO take from chest A UNLESS inventory full" stops taking when the golem can't carry more, so the next rule (deposit) runs.
pages.title: Order and Unless

rows: Always true. Use it last, as the fallback.
Any part's durability is under the percent.
Any part is at zero durability.
You are closer / farther than N blocks.
Something hurt you in the last 10 seconds.
A hostile mob is within N blocks and in sight.
More than N blocks from its post.
A ripe crop is within N blocks.
Chest A holds at least / fewer than N items.
A redstone signal at the golem or at its post.
It has left the work area marked with the Linker.
pages.title: WHEN...

rows: Walks to its post and stays.
Stands still. A higher rule can interrupt.
Wanders around its post (or where it is).
Fights the nearest hostile it can see.
Takes a stack per work cycle.
Stores a stack per work cycle.
The same with the nearest chest or barrel within 8 blocks.
Collects dropped items within 5 blocks (10 with Grabber Claws).
Harvests ripe crops and replants. Needs Scythe Arms or Grabber Claws.
Walks to a redstone block and charges.
Uses a Repair Kit from its inventory.
Walks into its linked Garage for a full repair.
Powers a Golem Signal Plate it stands on.
Hands its items to the nearest of your golems with room, within 12 blocks.
Walks between random spots inside its work area.
Walks onto its Golem Dock and rests, slowly recharging and healing.
pages.title: DO...

pages.text:
If an action can't run, the panel says why, such as "Stuck: no path to chest B" or "Stuck: chest A is empty".

If the same rule fails §lfive times§r in a row, the golem stops running rules, follows you, and shows "Stopped: ...". Editing its rules starts it again.
pages.title: Stuck and Stopped

pages.text:
The panel's activity list shows its last few jobs, so you can see what it has been up to.

Work has a short pause built in between items, shorter with faster arms.

§2§lTip:§r a big golem can't squeeze into a 1-wide gap. Leave 2 blocks of room around chests and crops.
pages.title: Activity

pages.text: The default: stays by your side and fights back for you.
pages.title: Follower

pages.text: Nothing to set up. Every new golem starts as a Follower.
pages.title: Setting It Up

pages.text: Holds a spot and attacks anything hostile that comes near.
pages.title: Guard

pages.text:
1. Shift + right-click the air with a Golem Linker until it says Post. 2. Right-click the spot to guard. 3. Right-click the golem with the Linker. 4. Choose Guard in its Rules tab.

§2§lTip:§r Hammer Arms hit every enemy nearby; a Scope Head spots them early.
pages.title: Setting It Up

pages.text: Moves everything from chest A to chest B, all day.
pages.title: Hauler

pages.text:
1. With the Linker in Chest A mode, right-click the chest to empty. 2. Switch to Chest B and click the chest to fill. 3. Optionally mark a Post to wait at. 4. Right-click the golem with the Linker and choose Hauler.

§2§lTip:§r Grabber Claws and a Cargo Barrel (27 stacks) make the best hauler. Place a redstone block nearby for recharging.
pages.title: Setting It Up

pages.text: Harvests and replants ripe crops, and stores them in the nearest chest.
pages.title: Harvester

pages.text:
1. Fit Scythe Arms (3 x 3 per swing) or Grabber Claws. 2. Place a chest within 8 blocks of the field. 3. Choose Harvester.

Works with wheat, carrots, potatoes, beetroot and nether wart (replanted), and pumpkins and melons (stem kept).

§2§lTip:§r a Lantern Head lets it work through the night.
pages.title: Setting It Up

pages.text: Looks after itself: patches up with Repair Kits and walks to the Garage when badly hurt.
pages.title: Medic

pages.text:
1. Build a Garage. 2. Linker in Garage mode: right-click the controller, then the golem. 3. Give it some Repair Kits and the materials its parts need. 4. Choose Medic.

Combine with other jobs: copy the top two rules into any golem's list.
pages.title: Setting It Up

pages.text: Follows you by day and stands watch at its post by night.
pages.title: Night Guard

pages.text:
Mark a post with the Linker (by your door, say) and choose Night guard.

§2§lTip:§r a Lantern Head lights up the area it guards, and a Soul Core keeps it healed.
pages.title: Setting It Up

pages.text:
Give a golem a §lwork area§r and it stays inside it: it only strolls, fights, picks up items and harvests within the area.

§l1.§r Shift + right-click the air with the Linker until it says Area corner 1, and click one corner. §l2.§r Switch to Area corner 2 and click the opposite corner. §l3.§r Right-click the golem.
pages.title: Marking an Area

pages.text:
While you hold a Linker you can see every golem's links and areas as colored outlines, and the marks the Linker itself is holding.

Use §loutside its area§r with §lpatrol its area§r to bring a golem back when it wanders off.
pages.title: Seeing Areas

pages.text: §2§lTip:§r an area over a farm plus "crop ready: harvest crops" keeps a harvester on its own field.

Golems can pass items to each other. A golem running §lgive to a golem§r walks to the nearest of §lyour§r golems that has room (within 12 blocks) and hands over its items, a stack at a time.

Golems that are themselves giving items are skipped, so two givers never pass the same items back and forth.
pages.title: Passing Items

rows: "inventory full: give to a golem", "crop ready: harvest crops"
"inventory full: deposit to chest B", "always: wait 5 s"
pages.title: Field to Storage

pages.text:
The harvester never leaves the field; the hauler with the Cargo Barrel does the walking to storage.

§2§lTip:§r give the hauler a Storage Module for 9 more stacks.
pages.title: Why It Works

pages.text:
Put golems in numbered §lgroups§r to set them up together.

§l1.§r Shift + right-click the air with the Linker until it says Group. §l2.§r Shift + scroll to pick a group, 1 to 9. §l3.§r Right-click golems to add them; shift + right-click takes one out.
pages.title: Making a Group

pages.text:
In a grouped golem's Rules tab, §lCopy to group§r saves its rules and gives a copy to every one of your golems in that group. Teach one harvester, and the whole crew knows the job.

The group number shows in the panel, in Jade and in /golemgarage list.
pages.title: Sharing Rules

pages.text:
Chest actions work with §lany block that stores items§r: chests, barrels, shulker boxes, hoppers, and storage from other mods such as drawers, crates, Create vaults and storage system interfaces.

The Linker's Chest A and Chest B modes accept them all, and "take from / deposit to chest" finds the nearest one within 8 blocks.
pages.title: Storage Blocks

rows: Furnace Chest + Furnace Core. Rules: "chest A has 1: take from chest A", "always: deposit to chest B". Put ore and coal in A; ingots come out in B.
Grabber Claws. "inventory full: deposit to chest", "always: pick up items". Clears mob farms and quarries.
"owner within 4: emit redstone" on a Signal Plate wired to a bell or door.
Lightning Core outdoors. "thunderstorm: go to post" under a lightning rod.
"raining: go to post" with the post under a roof stops weather wear.
pages.title: Ideas

categories.title: Upgrade Modules
categories.desc: Plug-in upgrades: two sockets per golem.

pages.text: Iron, copper and redstone make two casings.
pages.title: Module Casing

pages.text:
Every golem has §ltwo module sockets§r. Right-click a golem with a module to install it. A golem can't hold two of the same module.

To take one out, open the golem's panel: the Status tab shows both sockets with an x to remove each. The module comes back to you.

Modules stay in the golem when you pick it up.
pages.title: Sockets

rows: Pulls dropped items within 6 blocks into the golem's inventory.
Lights up everything around the golem.
Slowly mends worn parts, a little every 30 seconds.
pages.title: Every Module

pages.text: Pulls dropped items within 6 blocks into the golem's inventory.
pages.title: Magnet Module

pages.text: Lights up everything around the golem.
pages.title: Lamp Module

pages.text: Moves 20% faster.
pages.title: Speed Module

pages.text: Carries 9 more stacks (up to 36).
pages.title: Storage Module

pages.text: +6 armor and +10% knockback resistance.
pages.title: Plating Module

pages.text: Heals 1 health every 4 seconds.
pages.title: Regeneration Module

pages.text: Slowly mends worn parts, a little every 30 seconds.
pages.title: Self-Repair Module

categories.title: Tools and Blocks
categories.desc: The Golem Linker, Signal Plate, Blueprints, and other things you can use on a golem.

pages.text: An amethyst shard on two sticks.
pages.title: Golem Linker

pages.text:
The Linker tells golems where things are.

§l1.§r Shift + right-click the air to choose a mode: Post, Chest A, Chest B, Garage, Area corners, Home or Group. §l2.§r Right-click a block to mark it. Any storage block works for A and B; Garage needs a Garage Controller; Post and area corners mark the spot you click.
pages.title: Using It

pages.text:
§l3.§r Right-click a golem to give it every mark.

While you hold it, links and areas show as outlines.

The panel's Status tab lists each link and has §lPost here§r (sets its post where it stands) and §lClear links§r.

One Linker can hold every mark at once, so you can set up a hauler in one go. Shift + right-click a golem with the Linker to clear its links.
pages.title: From the Panel

pages.text: Iron, redstone, iron in a row.
pages.title: Golem Signal Plate

pages.text:
Outputs a redstone signal while a golem running §lemit redstone§r stands on it.

Use it to let golems open doors, ring bells, start machines, or tell your redstone that a job is done.

§2§lTip:§r put the plate at the golem's post and use "go to post" then "emit redstone" rules to signal on a schedule.
pages.title: Golems and Redstone

pages.text: Copper, a redstone block and iron.
pages.title: Golem Dock

pages.text:
A charging pad that gives a golem a home. Link it with the Linker in §lHome§r mode, then give the golem a §lrest at its dock§r rule, for example "night: rest at its dock".

While it stands on the dock it slowly recharges and heals, and the pad lights up.
pages.title: Home Sweet Home

pages.text:
Right-click a golem with any §ldye§r to paint its trim: the bands, plates and edges on every part. Use another dye to repaint.

Right-click with a §lwater bucket§r to wash the paint off. Paint is only for looks and is kept when you pick the golem up.
pages.title: Painting a Golem

pages.text: A book, redstone and paper.
pages.title: Blueprint

pages.text:
Use an §lempty blueprint§r on a golem to record its five parts (shape and material) and its rules.

Use a §lwritten blueprint§r on any golem to rebuild it: matching parts are taken from your inventory and fitted, the replaced parts come back to you, and the rules are copied.
pages.title: Copying a Build

categories.title: Cubs
categories.desc: Tiny chibi golems that follow you and carry your things.

pages.text: A slime ball, a chest and redstone. Place it with a right-click.
pages.title: Cub

pages.text:
Cubs are tiny golems with big heads, big eyes and a leaf sprout on top. They follow you everywhere, hop along behind, and can't be hurt.

If you get too far ahead, a Cub catches up by itself.
pages.title: Little Helpers

pages.text: Right-click with any dye to recolor it. Cubs start pink.
pages.title: Sixteen Colors

pages.text:
§lStorage§r: right-click a Cub with an empty hand to open its wardrobe and 9 pocket slots, or right-click while holding an item to hand it over.

§lItem magnet§r: it picks up items dropped within 3 blocks of it. Right-click with a §lfeather§r to turn the magnet off or on.

§lPick up§r: shift + right-click with an empty hand.
pages.title: Carrying

pages.text: It keeps its items, color and name.

Cubs have moods:

- They blink and tilt their heads at you.
- They §lsit§r when you crouch next to them.
- Stand still for a while and they §ldoze off§r, little z's floating up.
- Come back after being away and they §ljump around§r with hearts.
pages.title: Personality

pages.text:
Cubs can dress up. Craft an outfit piece and right-click a Cub with it, or open the Cub with an empty hand and put pieces in its §lwardrobe§r.

There are three slots: §lhead§r, §lbody§r and §laccessory§r. Taking a piece out gives it back.
pages.title: Dressing Up

pages.text: Caps, headphones, shades, jackets, hoodies and backpacks.
pages.title: Cool

pages.text: Witch hat, lace dress, spiked collar, vampire cape and bat wings.
pages.title: Goth

pages.text: Bunny ears, bows, frog hats, flower crowns, dresses, a bee costume, wings and a scarf.
pages.title: Cute

pages.text: A royal crown, a space helmet, a tuxedo, a monocle and a rocket jetpack.
pages.title: Fancy

pages.text:
Wear §lthree pieces of one style§r for a matching set. A Cub in a full set shows it off with its own sparkles: notes for cool, witchy swirls for goth, hearts for cute and glimmers for fancy.

Outfits go back to you if the Cub grows into a golem.
pages.title: Matching Sets

pages.text:
Feed a Cub §lthree golem parts§r, each for a different slot. After the third it grows into a full golem with those parts.

The new golem is yours and keeps the Cub's stored items.

The Cub tells you its progress: "Cub is growing: 2 / 3".
pages.title: Growing Up

categories.title: Optional Mods
categories.desc: Extra materials from All The Ores, Allthemodium and Silent Gear.

pages.text:
Nothing extra is needed to play. When another mod adds a metal this mod knows, that metal becomes a golem material automatically: recipes, the Parts tab and this book's crafting pages all pick it up.

Materials match by ingot tag, so any mod that adds, say, silver ingots works.
pages.title: Optional Mods

pages.text: A golem with parts from a mod that's later removed keeps them; they act as iron until the mod returns.
With All The Ores installed, these become golem materials. Click one to read about it.

pages.text: Server owners can change these in §lgolemgarage-server.toml§r (in the world's serverconfig folder, or the game's config folder for defaults).
pages.title: The Settings File

rows: How long a Garage repair takes (120).
Material the Garage charges per damaged part (1; 0 is free).
Rain and sand wear unsealed parts (on).
How fast golems use power (1; 0 never runs out).
Golems one player can have out (0 = no limit).
Golems allowed in one chunk (0 = no limit).
Jobs pause while the owner is offline or further than this (0 = off).
Others may pick up your golems and cubs (off).
Others may open, edit and link your golems (off).
Whether golems fight players: NEVER, PVP (default) or ALWAYS.
Golem kills drop XP and player loot as if the owner killed them (off).
Minutes a dropped golem or cub item lasts (0 = forever).

rows: Jobs golems can't use, such as harvest_crops.

Materials whose parts can't be fitted.
Per-material multipliers: "diamond;durability=2;speed=0.9". Stats: health, durability, speed, power, work, damage.

rows: How far a cub's item magnet reaches (3; 0 = off).

pages.title: Cubs and Commands

pages.text: Operators can always edit any golem, and skip the recall wait.
pages.title: Operators

pages.text: §l/golemgarage§r (or §l/gg§r) looks after your golems from anywhere. Name a golem by its name, its number in the list, or §lall§r.
pages.title: Commands

rows: Your golems: where they are, health, power and what they're doing. Click the coordinates to copy them.
Where it is, how far and which way. Loaded golems glow for 10 seconds.
Brings it to you, even from unloaded areas or another dimension.
Pauses its jobs, and starts them again.
pages.title: For Everyone

rows: A ready-built golem. Presets: standard, guard, hauler, harvester, medic, night_guard.
A cub in any dye color.
Fully repairs, heals and charges them.
How many golems the server has, by owner.
Removes all of a player's golems, even unloaded ones.
Its parts, links, rules and recent activity.
pages.title: For Operators

pages.text: §lDatapack materials§r: add a file at data/<pack>/golem_material/<id>.json with an item tag, a tier, a built-in material to borrow the look from, a tint color, optional stat multipliers and traits. Every part shape can then be crafted from it with the usual patterns, and the Garage repairs it with the same item.
pages.title: New Materials

pages.text:
§lItem tags§r: golemgarage:golem_parts (and golem_parts/head, torso, arms, legs, core), modules, outfits (and outfits/cool, goth, cute, fancy), golems, cubs, garage_blocks and tools. Use them in recipes, quests and filters.

The §l/golemgarage give§r presets make good quest rewards.
pages.title: Tags and Rewards

rows: The see-through build plan while holding a Garage Controller.
The little icons over golems that are stuck, stopped, out of power or have a broken part.
pages.title: golemgarage-client.toml

pages.text: Golem sounds are soft, fade out within 12 blocks, and get quieter when lots of golems are close together. §lgolemVolume§r (0 to 100) in golemgarage-client.toml turns golem and cub sounds down further, on top of the Friendly Creatures slider.
pages.title: Sounds

pages.text:
§lJEI§r: every part material, golem build and cub color shows as its own item, each item has an info page, and the Garage Controller shows §lGarage Repair§r recipes: what a worn-out golem costs to fix.

§lJade§r: look at a golem to see its power, what it's doing and its most worn part; look at a cub to see its outfit and matching set.
